localChanges: When a stronger civilization meets you, it now demands tribute sized to its strength and the difficulty level, and declares war if you refuse (closes #427).
A weaker or frightened civilization offers peace instead, and if you turn it down, sweetens the offer with an advance, then gold, then everything it has.
Once you are at peace, you can demand tribute in turn: a civilization that fears you pays, and one that doesn't ignores you.

Peace treaties now hold. Computer players no longer break one as soon as their army outnumbers yours, though one that only made peace because it was the weaker may quietly drop the treaty later (closes #71).
Computer players remember a sneak attack or a nuclear strike against them, and ask more and trust less of whoever did it.
Computer players settle war and peace between themselves by the original's rules, trading an advance each time they meet in peace.
